title: Late-time Radio and Millimeter Observations of Superluminous Supernovae and Long Gamma-Ray Bursts: Implications for Central Engines, Fast Radio Bursts, and Obscured Star Formation
question: Search for late-time non-thermal synchrotron radio and millimeter emission from superluminous supernovae (SLSNe) and long gamma-ray bursts (LGRBs) to constrain central engines (magnetar wind nebulae, off-axis relativistic jets), non-relativistic ejecta, fast radio bursts, and obscured star formation in host galaxies.

what.value: Existing radio observations of SLSNe from the literature (Table 1)

evidence.quote: Of these, 3 events were previously observed in the radio at early time, leading to non-detections: PTF09cnd (cite: Chandra2009; Chandra2010), SN2012il (cite: Chomiuk2012), and SN2015bn (cite: Nicholl2016a; Nicholl2018); see Table [\[tab:litslsne\]](#tab:litslsne).

external_data.citation: (cite: Schulze2018; Law2019; Chandra2009; Chandra2010; Chomiuk2011; Coppejans2018; Hatsukade2018; Eftekhari2019; Mondal2020; Chomiuk2012; Kasliwal2016; Nicholl2016b; Nicholl2018; Bright2017; Bose2018)

what.value: Inferred magnetar birth and ejecta properties (P, B, M_ej, E_K, v_ej) from MOSFiT optical light curve fits

evidence.quote: To model the PWN radio emission from each newborn SLSN remnant, we use the inferred magnetar birth properties (ejecta mass and velocity, magnetar magnetic field and spin period) from (cite: Nicholl2017b) and (cite: Blanchard2018)

what.value: Optically-inferred star formation rates (Halpha or SED modeling) of SLSN and LGRB host galaxies

evidence.quote: In Figure [2](#fig:sfrs), we compare the radio/mm-inferred upper limits on SFR to the SFRs derived from H$\alpha$ measurements or SED modeling (references are given in Appendix [\[appendix:a\]](#appendix:a)).

external_data.citation: (cite: Leloudas2015; Angus2016; Schulze2018; Lunnan2014; Perley2016a; Neill2011; Chen2013; Chen2015; Thone2015; Hatsukade2018; Chen2017; Anderson2018; Michaowski2012; Greiner2016; Niino2017; Levesque2010; Perley2015; Perley2013a)

recipe.goal: Extract continuum flux densities and image rms values from VLA and ALMA images
recipe.method: Use archival ALMA pipeline continuum images (and CASA-imaged VLA maps) and extract flux densities and rms noise at transient positions using pwkit imtool.
key_parameters: 3sigma upper limits for non-detections; 5sigma detection threshold

recipe.goal: Search Phased-VLA observations for fast radio bursts (FRBs)
recipe.method: Perform RFI excision with rfifind, incoherently dedisperse filterbank time series across 1000 trial DMs, remove red noise, and search scans with matched-filtering single_pulse_search.py.
key_parameters: DM up to 5000 pc cm^-3 with step size 5; 256 us time resolution; 2 MHz channels; 7sigma threshold
assumptions: Phasing efficiency factor of 0.9, nominal pulse width W = 10 ms, and beaming fraction f_b = 0.5

recipe.goal: Constrain obscured star formation rates in host galaxies and stack images
recipe.method: Calculate obscured SFR limits from 6 GHz and 100 GHz flux density limits using the k-corrected radio-SFR relation, and median-combine images centered on transient positions to constrain mean population SFRs.
key_parameters: Spectral index alpha = 0.75; median redshifts z approx 0.3 (LGRBs) and z approx 0.23 (SLSNe) for stacked limits
assumptions: Planck cosmological parameters: H_0 = 67.8 km s^-1 Mpc^-1, Omega_m = 0.308, Omega_Lambda = 0.692

recipe.method: Place limits on shock velocity and progenitor mass-loss rate for SLSNe using Chevalier (1998) synchrotron self-absorption model, and model spherical SN outflow light curves for LGRBs using Barniol Duran & Giannios (2015) and Kathirgamaraju et al. (2016).
key_parameters: For LGRB SNe: epsilon_e = epsilon_B = 0.1, p = 2.5, E_SN = 10^52 erg, v_ej = 8 x 10^3 km s^-1, n = 10 and 100 cm^-3
assumptions: Peak luminosity extrapolates back in time as L_nu,pk proportional to t^-1 for optically thin SLSN emission

recipe.goal: Constrain off-axis relativistic jets and minimum jet breakout energies
recipe.method: Generate a grid of 6 and 100 GHz off-axis jet afterglow light curves using Boxfit v2 to determine ruled-out (E_iso, n) space, and compute minimum jet breakout energy E_min from optical light curve kinetic energies E_K derived with MOSFiT.
key_parameters: theta_j = 10 deg; theta_obs = 30, 60, 90 deg; epsilon_e = 0.1; epsilon_B = 0.01; p = 2.5; f_j = 0.5

recipe.goal: Calculate free-free transparency timescales and model magnetar wind nebulae (ion-electron and electron-positron)
recipe.method: Compute free-free optical depth evolution at 6 and 100 GHz using CLOUDY, then compare radio/mm limits against ion-electron wind models (Margalit & Metzger 2018) and electron-positron PWN Boltzmann-equation models (Omand et al. 2018; Murase et al. 2016, 2020).
key_parameters: Broken power-law injection spectrum with q_1 = 1.5, q_2 = 2.5, and peak Lorentz factor gamma_b = 10^5 (and 10^4 for PTF10hgi)
assumptions: Energy injection rate L proportional to t^-2 in CLOUDY; singly-ionized oxygen ejecta for free-free absorption in electron-positron PWN model; no ejecta feedback

answer_key.quantity: 6 GHz flux density of PTF12dam host galaxy (first epoch, B-config)

evidence.quote: we detect radio emission near the location of the SLSN PTF12dam with a flux density $F_\nu = 117\pm 12 \ \mu$Jy; see Figure [1](#fig:ptf12dam).

answer_key.quantity: 6 GHz flux density of PTF12dam host galaxy (second epoch, A-config)

evidence.quote: Indeed, the emission is resolved out in our second epoch, A-configuration observation with a decreased flux density $F_\nu = 61.5 \pm 10.8 \ \mu$Jy, indicative of an extended source.

answer_key.quantity: 100 GHz 3sigma source flux density near SN2007bi (unrelated)

evidence.quote: We do not detect millimeter emission from any of our sources with the exception of a $3\sigma$ detection near the location of SN2007bi, with a flux density $F_\nu = 55.3 \pm 18.8 \ \mu$Jy

answer_key.quantity: 100 GHz luminosity upper limit for SN2018bsz

evidence.quote: We find that the majority of our limits are consistent with the model light curves invoked for PTF10hgi, although several deep limits at 100 GHz, most notably SN2018bsz with $L_\nu = 7.6\times 10^{26} \rm \ erg \ s^{-1} \ Hz^{-1}$, strongly rule out the presence of such nebulae.

answer_key.quantity: Minimum detectable FRB flux density (7sigma, 10 ms)

evidence.quote: no FRBs are detected to a limit of $16$ mJy ($7\sigma$; 10 ms duration) in about 40 min on source per event.

answer_key.quantity: Maximum FRB burst energy upper limits

evidence.quote: For the range of redshifts probed by our initial VLA sample of SLSNe ($z \sim 0.101 - 0.376$), we find $E_{\rm b,max} \lesssim 2 \times 10^{37} - 4 \times 10^{38}$ erg.

answer_key.quantity: Radio-inferred SFR of PTF12dam host galaxy

evidence.quote: In the case of PTF12dam, our radio detection of the host galaxy corresponds to an SFR of $6.7\pm 0.7 \ \rm M_{\odot} \ yr^{-1}$

answer_key.quantity: Stacked 100 GHz ALMA image rms for SLSNe

evidence.quote: The stacked ALMA image yields an rms of $3.7 \ \mu$Jy.

answer_key.quantity: Stacked 6 GHz VLA image rms for SLSNe

evidence.quote: We do not detect emission in either of the stacked populations, achieving 6 GHz rms values of about $2.6$ and $1.9$ $\mu$Jy for LGRBs and SLSNe, respectively.

answer_key.quantity: Stacked 6 GHz VLA image rms for LGRBs

evidence.quote: We do not detect emission in either of the stacked populations, achieving 6 GHz rms values of about $2.6$ and $1.9$ $\mu$Jy for LGRBs and SLSNe, respectively.

answer_key.quantity: Mean obscured SFR 3sigma limit for SLSNe from stacked 100 GHz image

evidence.quote: For the SLSNe, the $3\sigma$ SFR limits are $\lesssim 1.7$ and $\lesssim 27$ M$_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$ based on the 6 GHz ($z \approx 0.23$) and 100 GHz ($z \approx 0.23$) images, respectively.

answer_key.quantity: Mean obscured SFR 3sigma limit for SLSNe from stacked 6 GHz image

evidence.quote: For the SLSNe, the $3\sigma$ SFR limits are $\lesssim 1.7$ and $\lesssim 27$ M$_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$ based on the 6 GHz ($z \approx 0.23$) and 100 GHz ($z \approx 0.23$) images, respectively.

answer_key.quantity: Mean obscured SFR 3sigma limit for LGRBs from stacked 6 GHz image

evidence.quote: For the seven LGRBs in our sample, the non-detection corresponds to a $3\sigma$ limit of ${\rm SFR}\lesssim 4.2$ M$_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$ ($z\approx 0.3$).

answer_key.quantity: Minimum isotropic jet breakout energy range for SLSNe

evidence.quote: Finally, we note that the range of jet breakout energies ($E_{\rm min,iso} \approx 7 \times 10^{52} - 6 \times 10^{54}$ erg) for the SLSNe in our sample suggests that we do not expect a population of off-axis jets with energies comparable to the lowest energy LGRBs

answer_key.quantity: Free-free transparency timescale at 6 GHz for SLSNe

evidence.quote: Assuming that the energy injection rate into the nebula is given by $L \propto t^{-2}$, we find $t_{\rm ff}\approx 1.3 - 16.7$ yr at 6 GHz and $\approx 1.2 - 4.6$ yr at 100 GHz.

answer_key.quantity: Free-free transparency timescale at 100 GHz for SLSNe

evidence.quote: Assuming that the energy injection rate into the nebula is given by $L \propto t^{-2}$, we find $t_{\rm ff}\approx 1.3 - 16.7$ yr at 6 GHz and $\approx 1.2 - 4.6$ yr at 100 GHz.

not_stated_but_needed: Exact CASA version used for VLA processing and ALMA archival pipeline products
Exact ALMA array configurations and baseline ranges for the 2017 and 2019 campaigns
Exact pixel interpolation/regridding method used when median-combining ALMA images of different pixel scales (0.04-0.2 arcsec) and beam sizes for stacking
Exact fraction of magnetar spin-down power assumed to be deposited into ionizing radiation in the CLOUDY simulations
missing_for_reproduction: Exact CLOUDY input scripts and assumed ionizing radiation fraction of magnetar spin-down luminosity
Custom Boltzmann-equation PWN radiative transfer code from Omand et al. (2018) / Murase et al. (2020)
Exact Boxfit v2 configuration files and parameter grid resolution
Exact MOSFiT posterior chains for the newly fitted SLSNe (SN2010kd, SN2016els, SN2017gci, SN2017jan, SN2018hti, SN2018ibb)
score_reason: For the ALMA portion, the authors used standard archival pipeline products directly and measured rms/fluxes with a public tool (pwkit/imtool), making the observational measurements trivial to reproduce; however, the downstream theoretical modeling (CLOUDY scripts and custom PWN Boltzmann code) is not fully specified or publicly linked.
rediscovery_reason: Both ALMA project codes (2017.1.00280.S and 2019.1.01663.S) are public in the archive, the authors used the archive pipeline continuum images as-is, and all per-target rms values, 3sigma flux limits, and SFR limits are tabulated in Tables 3 and 4.
